\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 42\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Lifestyle and Nutritional Measures\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Follow-Up and Patient Education.\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Liver Transplantation\u003c/h4>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 43\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Complications of Upper Gastrointestinal Bleeding\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">1. Hemorrhagic Shock\u003cbr>2. Ongoing active hemorrhage\u003cbr>3. Acute Kidney Injury (AKI)\u003cbr>4. Prerenal AKI\u003cbr>5. Acute tubular necrosis\u003cbr>6. Hepatorenal syndrome\u003c/p>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 43\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,\">\u003cfigcaption>Figure · page 43\u003c/figcaption>\u003c/figure>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Rebleeding One of the most feared complications is: Recurrent bleeding Rebleeding\u003cbr>commonly occurs within: 72 hours after the initial hemorrhage.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">Aspiration for Pneumonia and Respiratory Failure\u003c/p>\u003ch4 class=\"note-text-block\">Hepatic Encephalopathy\u003c/h4>\u003c/section>\u003csection class=\"page-group\">\u003cdiv class=\"page-label\">PAGE 44\u003c/div>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">In cirrhotic patients, upper GI bleeding commonly precipitates: Hepatic encephalopathy\u003cbr>Blood proteins within the intestine are metabolized into: Ammonia which bypasses the\u003cbr>damaged liver through: portosystemic shunting,  and impaired hepatic detoxification.\u003c/p>\u003cp class=\"note-text-block\">This leads to: astrocyte swelling, neurotransmitter dysfunction and cerebral edema.\u003cbr>According to hepatology guidelines, GI bleeding is one of the commonest precipitants of\u003cbr>encephalopathy in cirrhosis.\u003c/p>\u003cfigure class=\"note-figure\">\u003cimg loading=\"lazy\" alt=\"Illustration associated with page 44\" src=\"data:image/webp;base64,
